rationale: Anytype documents a localhost API bundled with the desktop app, an official MCP server for AI assistants, and an agents skill that lets Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools 'read, search, and modify Objects' programmatically. The Anytype CLI runs Anytype as a headless server for automation, so no GUI is needed. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of agent read/write workflows (the evidence is vendor docs only, and the OpenAPI spec was not found at the probed doc.anytype.io paths).

A live probe confirms an llms.txt at doc.anytype.io (HTTP 200) that indexes the docs as raw .md pages, which an agent can ingest directly. The anytype-ts repo also ships an AGENTS.md, and there are agent-oriented skill docs for Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools. Missing for 10: no evidence of an llms.txt or llms-full.txt for the developer/API portal (developers.anytype.io), and no independent or hands-on corroboration of agents consuming these docs.

Anytype has no documented built-in AI that produces insights or suggestions. AI analysis of your data requires external tools: the official MCP server and the Agents Skill let assistants like Claude Code or Cursor read, search, and modify Objects through the local API. Queries and the Graph surface connections, but they are criteria-based and visual, not AI-generated. Missing for 10: native in-app AI insights or suggestions, any AI feature that runs inside the Anytype UI without third-party assistants, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

Anytype has no native automation engine, but it offers building blocks for one. The CLI can run Anytype as a headless server for automation and scripting, there is a local API, and external agents can run scripts against Anytype data for bulk edits and repetitive tasks. Autonomous background automations therefore depend on user-built scripts or third-party agent tools rather than a built-in feature. Missing for 10: native in-app automation rules/triggers, scheduling or background job execution, documentation of autonomous unattended workflows, and independent hands-on corroboration.

The evidence shows only external AI integrations: a local API, an MCP server, and an agents skill that you drop into Claude Code, Cursor, or similar tools so they can act on Anytype data. Nothing shows an AI assistant built into the Anytype app itself that users can delegate tasks to. The chat API covers ordinary messaging, not an assistant, and the 'AI Agents' mention on GitHub points to AGENTS.md rather than an in-app assistant.
